WHERE THIS WAS MEASURED vs WHERE IT LANDS. armed_commit is 08b7b05d9 - the commit the release
binary was built from, which is what the number is true of. The commit that lands this artifact is
its child: a lint fix in a unit test, plus a second parser barrier in `include_omit_names` found by
a probe AFTER the binaries were built (`include h` followed by `omit h` on the next line parsed as
one three-name command). That barrier is INERT on this slice by measurement, not by assumption:
exactly one line in all five pinned files starts with `include` or `omit` (Function/Basic:921
`include h`), and the line after it is blank, followed by `@[simp]` - an attribute token, which
stops the name run in the old code and the new one alike. The general rule from the previous
arming still applies and is still the conservative direction: the ratchet is monotonic-up, so a
baseline measured at an EARLIER commit can only be too low, never too high.

THE SLICE GREW FROM FOUR FILES TO FIVE at this commit, and one cap was retired.

1. `Mathlib/Order/Basic.lean` is the fifth pinned file (58/212). It was chosen on a
   MEASURED comparison against `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean` — both were checked end to end
   first, with the gate's own invocation — and not on reading. Order/Basic exercises a failure
   class the four Logic/Data foundations do NOT: over-application against a `Sort` head ("Too many
   arguments: function type Sort(Param ..) is not a function type") occurs 0 times in the pinned
   four (all 9 of their "Too many arguments" errors carry an FVar/App head) and 17 times here. It
   also populates all ten classes at once: its 25 `instance synthesis` failures are order-class
   instances (heads LE 8, LT 7, SDiff 3, Max 1, 6 unresolved), a structurally different source
   from Function/Basic's 28, and NONE of its 20 `unknown identifier` failures is a cascade marker.
   Group/Defs measured 15/265 with 82 "other", 62 of them that same Sort-head class, but 25 of its
   48 `unknown identifier` failures are "attribute target ... not found in environment" — i.e.
   downstream of one early wall rather than independent frontier — so it re-measures one wall
   where Order/Basic maps five. It is the recommended SIXTH file, already measured, not a
   rejected one. Its
   contrast with the olean lane is worth keeping in view: docs/plans/MATHLIB_KV_MILESTONE_2026-07-12.md
   records Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs at 1123/1123 KernelVerified through .olean IMPORT, against
   15/265 through SOURCE elaboration — the same declarations, and the gap is the elaborator.

   The choice paid for itself immediately: Order/Basic surfaced a defect the four-file slice
   could not have found. `end A.B` pops ONE namespace component instead of the whole dotted
   path, so every declaration after such a pair is registered under a wrong fully-qualified
   name and the residue accumulates — 151 of Order/Basic's 153 named errors (86% of all 175
   failures) are reported against a mis-qualified name. The pinned four declare NO dotted
   namespace at all, which is why they never saw it. Minimal repro, blast radius, and the
   measurement that the causal share is ZERO (desugaring all four dotted namespace/end pairs
   in that file leaves success and failed bit-for-bit identical at 58/212 and 175) are in
   docs/issues/2026-08-23-end-dotted-namespace-pops-one-component.md — read it before budgeting
   any source-elab gain against that fix.

2. `Mathlib/Logic/Unique.lean` is pinned UNCAPPED (8/41); the key
   `Mathlib/Logic/Unique.lean:1-240` (baseline 8, decl_count 35) is retired. The cap existed
   because docs/plans/SOURCE_ELAB_IMPORTS_2026-07-13.md recorded the final section (lines 241-270)
   OOMing at ~19.5 GB. THAT OOM NO LONGER REPRODUCES: measured 2026-08-23 under a 1 Hz RSS sampler
   with a hard 20 GiB kill cap, the full 270-line file peaks at 2.97 GiB and completes in 243 s,
   against 2.90 GiB / 229 s for a 239-line control — the blamed tail costs +0.07 GiB and +14 s.
   The tail's own diagnostics say why: Unique.subtypeEq/subtypeEq' now fail FAST inside `congr`
   ("goal mismatch: congr: functions on both sides must be equal", "type check failed:
   TypeMismatch") instead of searching, and Fin.instUnique fails on "Missing field(s) for
   Inhabited: default". The retired key's 8 is NOT lost and is not weakened: the uncapped key
   measures exactly 8 too, over a strict superset — decl_count 35 -> 41, i.e. six
   declarations that the cap was hiding are now measured, and all six fail. The gate's `head -n <cap>` machinery stays and is still tested
   (test 11b of scripts/test_source_elab_gate.sh drives it generically), it simply has no user.

HOW A FILE CAN BE ADDED AT ALL. Before this change the armed-ratchet fail-closed rule
(failed:ratchet-missing-key) also applied to `--update`, so a newly pinned file could only be armed
by first hand-typing a placeholder baseline into this artifact — exactly the un-evidenced number
that --check-artifact's evidence binding exists to forbid. `--update` now arms an unbaselined
pinned file FROM ITS MEASUREMENT and says so on stdout; a run WITHOUT --update still fails closed.

(151/77/13/8). The armed ratchet has now held across three commits.

Per-file success_baseline is monotonic-up: the gate fails
(SRCELAB_GATE=failed:ratchet-regression) if any pinned file drops below it, --update refuses to
lower an armed baseline, and an armed ratchet with a pinned file that has NO entry fails closed
(failed:ratchet-missing-key) on any run that is not an --update.

counting_basis=allow_sorry_success because Clean-check-report-v1 (crates/clean-cli/src/cmd_core.rs)
carries NO per-decl sorry-taint field: under --allow-sorry, sorry-tainted decls are folded into
success_count (record_checked_decl) and taint is only visible as the run-wide
trust_summary.sorry_axioms counter, recorded per file above. A strict per-decl sorry-free basis
needs a companion run WITHOUT --allow-sorry, where sorry decls surface individually in
trust_failures — tracked follow-up; do not present allow_sorry_success as sorry-free.

A LEAD ON THAT FOLLOW-UP, found while arming this slice: the second run may not be needed at
all. `clean check --verbose` ALREADY prints the taint per declaration — Order/Basic's tick list
reads `✓ <name> (sorry allowed)` for exactly 5 of its 58 successes, matching its
trust_summary.sorry_axioms of 5 to the declaration. So the strict sorry-free basis is 53/212 for
that file, and what is missing is not a measurement but a FIELD: the verbose printer knows the
bit that Clean-check-report-v1 does not serialise. Plumbing it into the JSON would give a strict
per-decl basis from the same single run this gate already pays for.
